claims.text: Adding a controlled amount of boron to refractory high-entropy alloys can improve their high-temperature mechanical capability.
Boron addition can limit density increase while preserving room-temperature performance.
Boron addition causes boride precipitates to form in refractory high-entropy alloys.
Boride precipitates act as pinning points for dislocations.
Dislocation pinning by boride precipitates enhances creep resistance.
Dislocation pinning by boride precipitates improves high-temperature strength.
The boron-containing alloy will have at least 10% greater high-temperature yield strength than an otherwise relevant alloy without boron.
The yield-strength improvement will occur without a significant increase in density.
The yield-strength improvement will occur while preserving room-temperature ductility.
The beneficial effect of boron addition should hold above 1000°C under loading relevant to jet-turbine applications.
The beneficial effect of boron addition will be most pronounced between 1000°C and 1200°C under stresses typical of jet-turbine components.
